grants.description: Verify your identity using your NHS login or GOV.UK One Login credentials
grants.purpose: To confirm you are who you say you are before processing your exemption application

grants.description: Check your benefit status with the Department for Work and Pensions
grants.purpose: To verify if you are receiving qualifying benefits (PIP, DLA, ESA, UC) that entitle you to free prescriptions

grants.description: Access your NHS medical records to verify qualifying medical conditions
grants.purpose: To confirm diagnosis of qualifying medical conditions (diabetes, epilepsy, thyroid conditions, etc.) that entitle you to free prescriptions

grants.description: Contact your GP to verify your medical condition and ongoing treatment
grants.purpose: To obtain clinical confirmation of your qualifying medical condition and that you require continuous treatment

grants.description: Share your exemption certificate details with NHS Business Services Authority
grants.purpose: To issue your medical exemption certificate (MedEx) and record it in the NHS exemption checking system

revocation.mechanism: Contact NHS Business Services Authority or revoke through your NHS account
revocation.effect: Application will be cancelled if consent is revoked before completion. Existing exemption certificates remain valid until expiry date.

delegation.limitations: Agent cannot approve medical evidence without clinical verification from a qualified healthcare professional. Agent cannot override GP assessment of medical conditions. Agent cannot issue exemption certificates for medical conditions without documented clinical evidence. Agent must handoff to human clinician if medical condition requires assessment.
